title: The Corp That Paid Farmers to Burn Crops—Then Sold Food Aid
hook: A global agribusiness secretly financed the destruction of surplus grain to keep prices high, then billed USAID for famine relief shipments.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines moral outrage with a 'they caused the very disaster they profited from' twist—perfect for outrage-driven sharing.

title: The Trader Who Used a Dead Satellite to Fake Crop Data
hook: A hedge fund bought a decommissioned satellite in a junkyard, retasked its sensors, and leaked false drought images to drive wheat futures.
why_this_can_go_viral: Space-age scam with a junkyard origin—extremely visual and counterintuitive, perfect for conspiracy-curious audiences.

title: The Startup That Sold Fake Identities to Fortune 500s—Then Blackmailed Them
hook: A background-check startup built dossiers on its own clients and used the dirt to extort multimillion-dollar 'consulting fees.'
why_this_can_go_viral: Reverse betrayal—company trusts a vendor, vendor weaponizes the trust. Classic 'how the turn tables' narrative.

title: The Spy Who Faked a Factory Fire to Steal a Competitor's Recipe
hook: A corporate spy doused a rival's facility with accelerant, set a controlled fire, and walked in with firefighters to 'discover' the secret formula.
why_this_can_go_viral: Arson as a cover for espionage—high-stakes, cinematic, feels like a heist movie.

title: The Ad Agency That Bought Psychic Hotlines—Then Trained Operators to Sell
hook: A marketing firm purchased bankrupt psychic hotlines, replaced readers with scripted salespeople, and sold timeshares to lonely callers.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exploits loneliness and superstition—gut-wrenching and ethically repulsive, drives anger-based shares.

title: The Factory That Sold 'Wild Salmon'—It Was Genetically Modified Tilapia Dyed Pink
hook: A seafood processor imported GMO tilapia from a factory farm, injected color additives, and labeled it 'Alaskan wild salmon.'
why_this_can_go_viral: Gross-out reveal that makes people question everything they eat—high disgust-reaction sharing.

title: The Oil Company That Paid Scientists to Fake Climate Data for 20 Years
hook: A major oil firm funded a shadow lab that produced 'neutral' climate models, then leaked them to journalists as independent science.
why_this_can_go_viral: Timeless outrage fuel—taps into deep distrust of big oil and climate change denial.

title: The Trader Who Faked a CEO's Death—With a Doctored Autopsy Report
hook: A short seller forged a coroner's report claiming a pharma CEO died of a rare disease, tanked the stock, then bought the dip.
why_this_can_go_viral: Morbid, audacious, and legally insane—combines crime, finance, and a 'too dark to be fiction' vibe.

title: The Startup That Sold 'Cancer Cures'—It Was Sugar Pills and Chemo Rebottled
hook: A biotech startup raised $200M for a miracle cancer drug—it was repackaged chemotherapy from overseas, cut with placebo pills.
why_this_can_go_viral: Preys on desperate patients—maximum emotional impact, guaranteed outrage and shock.

title: The Monopoly That Bought All the Dental Clinics—Then Filled Cavities With Cement
hook: A private equity firm rolled up hundreds of dental chains, replaced fillings with cheap construction cement, and billed insurance for gold.
why_this_can_go_viral: Body horror meets corporate greed—makes people physically cringe, highly shareable disgust.

title: The Spy Who Stole a Car Engine Blueprint by Burying a Bug in a Test Track
hook: A competitor's agent buried a seismic sensor beneath a proving ground and reverse-engineered engine vibrations into CAD files.
why_this_can_go_viral: Spy tech meets automotive—feels like a real-world James Bond gadget story.

title: The Ad Agency That Used a Fake Church to Sell Donation Data to 500 Brands
hook: A marketing firm registered a nonprofit church, collected 'tithing' data from millions, and sold the donor lists to credit card companies.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exploits religion for profit—extremely controversial, guaranteed to shock believers and secular audiences alike.

title: The Factory That Sold 'Premium' Beef—It Was Horsemeat and Gelatin Binders
hook: A European slaughterhouse mixed horse meat with beef trimmings and gelatin to create 'prime cuts' sold to budget supermarkets for a decade.
why_this_can_go_viral: Classic 'what's in your food?' reveal—disgust-driven, taps into distrust of processed meat.

title: The Pharma Corp That Invented a Disease to Sell a Drug—Then Killed Patients
hook: A drug manufacturer fabricated a syndrome, got it listed in medical textbooks, and marketed a treatment that caused liver failure in children.
why_this_can_go_viral: Medical conspiracy at its darkest—sickening, true, and makes people question the entire healthcare system.

title: The Trader Who Bought a Weather Station—Then Faked a Hurricane Warning
hook: A commodities trader purchased a private weather station, transmitted a false hurricane alert, and shorted orange juice futures before the 'storm' fizzled.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exploits nature and fear—clever, illegal, and deeply satisfying for audiences who love 'how they got caught' stories.

title: The Startup That Sold 'Live' Customer Support—It Was a Chatbot With a Scripted Actor
hook: A customer service startup raised millions with a 'human-first' AI—every agent was a low-paid actor following a script, told to hide the truth.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exposes the 'AI hype bubble'—makes people feel cheated, drives shares from skeptical tech communities.

title: The Monopoly That Owned All the Seed—Then Made Farmers Pay to Grow Their Own Crop
hook: A seed giant patented a gene, cornered 90% of a staple crop, then sued farmers whose fields were 'contaminated' by wind-blown pollen.
why_this_can_go_viral: David vs. Goliath story—outrage against corporate control of food supply, highly shareable in farming communities.

title: The Spy Who Posed as a Journalist to Steal a Formula From a Rival Lab
hook: A corporate mole got hired as a science reporter, toured a competitor's facility, and secretly recorded the entire manufacturing process.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exploits the trust in journalism—deeply cynical, feels like a spy thriller.

title: The Ad Agency That Programmed Vending Machines to Scare Kids Into Buying Soda
hook: A marketing firm installed facial-recognition cameras in school vending machines that played scary sounds if kids didn't buy a drink.
why_this_can_go_viral: Predatory targeting of children—maximum outrage, parents will share aggressively.

title: The Factory That Sold 'Pure' Spring Water—It Was Tap Water From a Superfund Site
hook: A bottling plant pumped groundwater from a polluted industrial zone, filtered it minimally, and sold it as 'natural spring water' for 20 years.
why_this_can_go_viral: Gross betrayal of consumer trust—makes people rethink every bottle they've bought.

title: The Insurance Corp That Paid Hitmen to Kill Policyholders—Then Collected
hook: An offshore insurer wrote life policies on homeless people, then hired assassins to make it look like accidents, cashing millions in payouts.
why_this_can_go_viral: Absolute moral event horizon—shock value is off the charts. Guaranteed to spread like wildfire.

title: The Trader Who Faked a Tanker Explosion—Using a Drone and a Barrel of Oil
hook: A speculator launched a drone with a firebomb at an empty tanker, broadcasted 'explosion' footage, and shorted crude before the truth emerged.
why_this_can_go_viral: High-tech, high-stakes, and looks like a Michael Bay movie—perfect for adrenaline-driven shares.

title: The Startup That Sold 'Homes for Veterans'—It Was a Forever Lease With No Ownership
hook: A housing startup promised affordable homes to vets—the fine print gave them no deed, only a lease that expired after their death.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exploits patriotism and vulnerability—deeply infuriating, patriotic audiences will share widely.

title: The Corp That Bought All the Milk—Then Poured It Into the Ocean to Raise Prices
hook: A dairy conglomerate secretly purchased tens of millions of gallons of milk and dumped them at sea to create a 'shortage' and spike prices.
why_this_can_go_viral: Visual of milk pouring into ocean—waste + greed + environmental harm, triple outrage trigger.
